schools.text: He pledged to fight for strong public schools.
schools.quote: I will fight for affordable healthcare, strong public schools, and an economy that works for working families, not just those with power and influence.

abortion.text: He supports codifying the right to abortion in federal law.
abortion.quote: I support codifying the right to abortion in federal law. Politicians need to stay out of decisions between doctors and patients.

health.text: He supports universal single-payer health care through Medicare for All.
health.quote: We need universal, single-payer healthcare with no out-of-pocket costs.

tax.text: His campaign calls for lower taxes and disciplined federal spending.
tax.quote: New Jersey families need lower costs, lower taxes, and accountable government—not another blank check.

debt.text: He says Medicare reforms should keep commitments to seniors while addressing waste, fraud, and abuse.
debt.quote: For Medicare, we must keep our promises to seniors. Reforms should focus on eliminating waste, fraud, and abuse

schools.text: His campaign’s education framework includes school choice alongside local control and curriculum transparency.
schools.quote: Gregg’s education framework calls for curriculum transparency, local control, school choice, vocational and technical education, strong science and mathematics, and serious instruction in American civics.

safety.text: His campaign says it supports law enforcement and calls for enforcing the law and securing the border.
safety.quote: Secure the border, enforce the law, support law enforcement, and protect New Jersey neighborhoods from policies that put ideology first.

guns.text: In an older candidate questionnaire, he disagreed with the statement that more restrictive gun control is needed for public safety.
guns.quote: More restrictive gun control is needed to protect public safety.

abortion.text: In an older candidate questionnaire, he agreed that human life begins at conception and deserves legal protection.
abortion.quote: Human life begins at conception and deserves legal protection at every stage until natural death.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: In an older candidate questionnaire, he strongly disagreed with allowing restroom and changing-room access based on gender identity.
gender.quote: People should be allowed to use public restrooms, showers, and changing rooms based on "gender identity."

cannabis.text: He answered that he strongly agrees with legalizing recreational marijuana.
cannabis.quote: I support the legalization of recreational marijuana. Strongly Agree

health.text: His campaign favors competition and patient choice and opposes replacing the current system with a single federal payer.
health.quote: The campaign supports greater price transparency, more competition, portability, and targeted reforms intended to give patients more information and more choice rather than replacing the current system with a single federal payer.

energy.text: His campaign supports reliable, affordable energy, including dispatchable generation, nuclear power, and natural gas.
energy.quote: Gregg’s Affordable Energy Commitment supports reliable, dispatchable generation; nuclear power and natural gas alongside competitive emerging technologies; faster permitting for responsible domestic energy and grid infrastructure; and clear disclosure of subsidies, transmission expenses, and other policy-driven costs borne by taxpayers or ratepayers.

voting.text: He strongly disagreed that people should be able to vote without photo identification.
voting.quote: People should be able to vote without photo identification. Strongly Disagree

tax.text: He proposes shifting more of the tax burden to top earners while funding social programs.
tax.quote: Shift the burden of taxation to the top 1% of earners and eliminate income taxes for middle and lower income households.

wages.text: He proposes raising the federal minimum wage to $25 an hour, indexing it to inflation, and requiring service workers to receive the full minimum wage in addition to tips.
wages.quote: Raise the federal minimum wage from $7.25 to $25 an hour and index future increases to inflation.

housing.text: He proposes major public housing investment, with a goal of making 60% of the market high-quality, income-based social housing.
housing.quote: Major public housing investment with a goal to make 60% of the market high-quality, income-based units i.e. social housing.

schools.text: He proposes federal funding for local schools and after-school programs instead of relying on property taxes.
schools.quote: Fund local schools and after-school programs at the federal level rather than through property taxes.

safety.text: He proposes treating drug possession and use as public health issues, decriminalizing victimless offenses, and ending private prisons and detention centers.
safety.quote: Treat drug possession and use as public health issues; decriminalize victimless offenses.

immigration.text: He proposes a new amnesty, transferring immigration courts to the federal judiciary, and shutting down detention centers as part of an immigration overhaul.
immigration.quote: A complete overhaul of the immigration system, which includes a new amnesty, transfer of courts to the federal judiciary, shutting down detention centers, and more efficient processes

abortion.text: He supports codifying the right to bodily autonomy and access to abortion into law.
abortion.quote: Codify into law the right to bodily autonomy and access to abortion.

cannabis.text: He supports federally legalizing marijuana and ensuring cannabis dispensaries can access banking services.
cannabis.quote: Legalize marijuana federally and ensure cannabis dispensaries have access to banking services.

health.text: He supports free, single-payer universal healthcare for everyone, regardless of immigration status.
health.quote: Free single-payer universal healthcare available to everyone, regardless of status.

energy.text: He proposes a full transition to a decarbonized economy powered by 100% renewable energy.
energy.quote: Fund a full transition to a decarbonized economy powered by 100% renewable energy.

schools.text: Jordan supports increasing public school funding and protecting K–12 district funding.
schools.quote: On education, we must increase public school funding, make college affordable, expand vocational training, and aid workers displaced by automation.

immigration.text: Jordan supports a citizenship pathway for undocumented immigrants and protections for DACA recipients.
immigration.quote: I support a direct pathway to citizenship for undocumented immigrants, permanent DACA protection, an end to for-profit detention, and decriminalized border crossings with humane asylum processing.

guns.text: Jordan supports universal background checks, assault-weapon restrictions and red-flag laws.
guns.quote: Winston Jordan supports comprehensive, evidence-based gun safety reforms to reduce violence and protect communities.

abortion.text: Jordan supports nationwide legal access to abortion and opposes state bans or restrictions.
abortion.quote: I support full access to abortion, contraception, fertility treatment, and maternal care without restriction, stigma, or cost barriers.

gender.text: Jordan opposes blanket bans excluding transgender women from women's sports and public spaces.
gender.quote: Winston Jordan strongly disagrees with blanket bans excluding transgender women from women's sports and public spaces.

health.text: Jordan supports Medicare for All and a district pilot expanding health coverage through the VA network.
health.quote: The U.S. faces six critical challenges. On economic inequality, I propose the American Economic Security Act: a $50K minimum livable income, Employer of Last Resort program, and $50B wealth cap—using demand-side economics to stimulate growth. On climate change, we need renewable energy investment, carbon pricing, sustainable infrastructure, and environmental justice. On healthcare, I support Medicare-for-All, expanded mental health and opioid treatment, and protected reproductive rights.

energy.text: Jordan supports renewable energy investment, carbon pricing and sustainable infrastructure to address climate change.
energy.quote: On climate change, we need renewable energy investment, carbon pricing, sustainable infrastructure, and environmental justice.

voting.text: He supports automatic voter registration for U.S. citizens.
voting.quote: States must automatically register US Citizens to vote. implement blockchain technology to prevent hacking.

sources: hamawyfornj.com · mele4america.com · ballotready.org · ivoterguide.com · andresjinete.org · onyourballot.vote411.org
